title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week

    . This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Positive

Large-cap indices continue to build on their recent momentum, stacking up positive price action above rising 10- and 20-day moving averages and now posting two consecutive closes above their 50-day moving averages — a key technical milestone.

Mid- and small-cap indices are following closely, having just broken above their respective 50-day moving averages as of Friday’s close. As long as the major indices hold these rising short-term moving averages and continue forming higher lows and higher highs, the market trend remains healthy and constructive. This kind of orderly price action, supported by expanding participation, reflects growing institutional confidence.

Breadth and momentum indicators continue to register strong positive readings, supporting the case for a broad-based advance. The ratio of advancing to declining stocks, along with expanding upside momentum across market caps, suggests demand is sustaining and broadening out.

A notable development is the resurgence of Technology, which has delivered strong gains over the past several sessions. After lagging for months, Tech has now moved to the top of the sector performance rankings. This shift signals an increased risk appetite among investors, favoring growth-oriented areas — a constructive signal for the broader market.

Risk Management and Exposure Control

  • Maintain a Constructively Bullish Bias: With major indices holding above rising 10-, 20-, and now 50-day moving averages, market structure has improved. A cautiously bullish stance is now appropriate.

  • Gradually Increase Exposure: Begin scaling into high-quality setups as confirmation builds. Position sizes can be increased modestly while keeping risk management protocols in place.

  • Exit or Reduce Underperformers: Continue to trim or close lagging positions that aren’t participating in the uptrend. Rotate into names showing leadership or technical strength.

Market Monitoring and Internal Indicators

  • Watch for Trend Continuation:

    • Higher highs and higher lows across indices suggest healthy price structure.

    • Sustained closes above the 50-day moving average will further validate the intermediate-term trend.

  • Monitor Internal Strength:

    • Breadth and momentum should remain supportive. Continued outperformance in advancing issues and positive momentum across market caps indicate robust participation.

    • A deterioration in internals without corresponding strength in price action would warrant caution.

Sector and Theme Development

  • Focus on Strength in Growth-Oriented Sectors:

    • Technology’s emergence as a leader is a significant shift. Monitor this sector closely for continuation and supporting names.

    • Watch Consumer Discretionary and Semiconductors for potential follow-through in the growth space.

  • Track Leadership Rotation:

    • Defensive sectors are rotating lower in relative strength rankings. Avoid over-allocating to areas losing momentum.

    • Seek out early relative strength in previously lagging but now-improving sectors.

Capital Allocation and Trade Execution

  • Prioritize High-Probability Setups:

    • Favor clean breakouts, base patterns, and retests of moving averages with strong volume support.

    • Look for stocks forming constructive pullbacks or flag patterns above key MAs.

  • Maintain Clear Risk Boundaries:

    • Use logical stop-loss levels below recent support or moving averages.

    • Only scale up if setups show follow-through and market conditions remain supportive.

Daily Reassessment and Adaptive Strategy

  • Assess Key Benchmarks:

    • Watch how indices react to short-term pullbacks. Strong support at rising 10/20-day MAs would signal healthy demand.

    • Monitor whether the breadth of participation continues to expand or starts to narrow.

  • Adjust Exposure Accordingly:

    • If internals remain strong and indices advance, increase exposure into strong names.

    • If indices roll over or internals weaken, tighten exposure and reevaluate.

Key Focus Areas

  • Patience with Confirmation: Don’t chase extended names — wait for pullbacks, retests, or secondary entries.

  • Focus on Setup Expansion: The growing number of high-quality bases and breakouts is a positive. Let them guide your stock selection more than index direction alone.

  • Stay Nimble and Objective: Even in improving markets, conditions can shift quickly. Maintain flexibility to adapt as needed.

Bottom Line

The market has taken an important technical step forward, with improving internals, reclaiming of moving averages, and emerging risk-on leadership from technology. While caution is still warranted due to potential resistance ahead, the environment now supports a more proactive yet disciplined trading posture.
